name: generate_scene
description: Generates ONE TILE of the continuous world in Map Format D: declarative primitives (`ground` + `volumes`) plus a list of named entities with cell + footprint. You never write a `size` or a `terrain[]` grid — the engine synthesises the 128x128 @0.5 m grid from the `biome` and your primitives, and a scene that carries either is REJECTED. The narrative engine reads the result to know what is where; the game engine renders it in first person, at eye level over the tile. See system prompt for the full schema and a worked example.

scene_id.description: Unique slug identifying this map (e.g. 'tile_0_0' for a world tile).

place_id.description: The world-map place id this scene realizes; the engine binds the scene to that place. Optional.

scene_description.description: 2-3 sentence description of the scene, in Spanish.

terrain_legend.description: Mapping from terrain char to terrain name. Only for CUSTOM chars your primitives introduce (a structure's wall_char/floor_char of your own); reserved chars need no entry, and an undeclared char is rejected. A value can also be {"name": ..., "solid": true|false} to declare that char blocks movement. W and w are solid by default; b (bridge) is walkable.

ground.description: Ground features as typed objects (max 64), coordinates in cells 0..128: path {points:[[c,r],...], w?, material?}, area {rect|polygon|ellipse, material}, water {rect|polygon|ellipse} (blocks movement), deck {rect|polygon|ellipse, material?} (walkable OVER water, punches its collision), hill {rect|polygon|ellipse, h: METRES, -6..6 non-zero} (smooth declared relief: positive knoll, negative hollow; presentation-only — collision stays flat, it flattens under buildings/paths/areas/water and dies at tile seams; first-person view only today). Area-like kinds take EXACTLY ONE shape. Anything BUILT with height goes in "volumes". See MAP PLAN in the tile instructions.

vegetation_zones.description: OPTIONAL (tiles) — mass vegetation planted BY THE ENGINE as REAL tree/bush volumes (trunk collision, shade, everything a hand-placed tree volume has): [{type: Spanish plant name ('pino', 'matorral'…), area: [col,row,w,h] in cells | "rest" (the whole tile), density: SPECIMENS PER m² in (0, 0.08] — 0.01 open oakwood (100 stems/ha), 0.05 mature forest, 0.08 closed pinewood, seed?: string to reshuffle the same zone}] (max 8 zones). The engine plants them deterministically, keeps at least 2.58 m between trunks so the player can always walk through, and avoids paths, water, decks and building footprints automatically; your declared tree volumes act as spacing seeds. The zone spends the tile's volume budget (200 composed volumes per tile — see volumes_total/volumes_total_cap in the validator's stats): a "rest" zone at 0.08 asks for ~328 specimens and does NOT fit; the same density over HALF the tile does (~164), and a whole-tile forest fits at 0.04 (~164). This is the tool for forests and shrub masses; hand-place only singular specimens. For visual filler with NO collision and no budget, use scatter_zones instead.

volumes.description: Everything with HEIGHT as typed objects (building/wall/tower/gate/tree/bush/rock/fountain/prop, `prism` for a free polygon outline + height, or `custom` for a FREE 3D composition: any object built from solid pieces — box/cylinder/cone/sphere/gable with local pos/rot/scale and colors, optional per-piece `desc` — the SURFACE of that piece's faces seen square-on, painted literally into its texture cell (the object's other pieces are separate geometry)) with footprint in cells + height; the engine builds them as 3D volumes and derives collision from the footprints. See the MAP PLAN section of the system prompt. Buildings, rect-props and customs accept `angle` (degrees, CCW from above): the rotated footprint drives collision and manifest. building/wall/prop/prism accept optional `surface_desc` for the first-person view — painted once as a unique texture that joins the reusable surface library. The description is the flat SURFACE of the faces it covers (seen square-on), painted literally. Either a string (<=200 chars: one texture for the BODY's side faces; roof/doors keep their derived material) or an object with a DIFFERENT description per face/role (keys n|s|e|w|side|roof|door|caps|top). Each description is its own asset; without one, surfaces derive from material/color. Volumes with surface_desc also accept surface_ref (optional): id of a themed reference image from world.style_refs.fps_faces guiding how the style paints that face (string = all described faces; object = per face).

scatter_generators.description: OPTIONAL (first-person view) — procedural filler generators as pure JSON: { "<kind>": { vars?, materials?, parts:[{shape:"box"|"cylinder"|"cone"|"sphere", mat?, seg?, pos?:[x,y,z] (y=BASE, cells), scale?, rotX?|rotY?|rotZ?, repeat?:{count}, vars?, + the shape's dims}] } }. Numeric fields accept literal | [min,max] | {var} | {int:[a,b]} | {op,a,b} | {lerp:[a,b]} (inside repeat). See the SCATTER section of the MAP PLAN instructions. Instances do not collide and cost no image credits.

scatter_zones.description: OPTIONAL, requires scatter_generators — zones to populate: [{kind, shape: {type:"rect",x0,z0,x1,z1}|{type:"ellipse",cx,cz,rx,rz}|{type:"poly",pts}, density (elements/m², 0..1.5; total capped at 240 instances/tile), seed?}] (cells; max 12). The engine samples deterministic positions avoiding buildings, water, decks and paths automatically.

entities.description: Every thing on the map that is NOT terrain.

cell.description: [col, row] of the top-left of the footprint.

shape.description: Optional footprint shape hint (default box). cylinder = round (barrel/well/round tower/urn/fountain), sphere = boulder/dome, cone = tent/spire/pile, box = buildings/walls/crates.

h.description: Optional real-world height in METRES (NOT cells — footprint stays in cells). Guide: house 2.5-4, tower/church 5-8, tree 3-8, prop 0.5-2, item/decor ~0.5. Omit to use the per-kind default (building 2.5, tree 4, prop 1, item/decor 0.5).

attach.description: decor only: snap to the nearest wall cell (torches, signs, banners).

role.description: NPCs only, optional: BEHAVIOUR preset the simulation runs for this NPC (guard stands its ground and steps into a fight; peasant/villager/merchant wander and flee; `hostile` ATTACKS the player — the engine derives its health, weapon and aggression, you do not). It is NOT the job — a smith, a mayor or an innkeeper are villagers/merchants who happen to have a trade, and the trade goes in `name` and `description`; a bandit, a wolf or a cultist are `hostile` and their identity goes there too. Same five values as spawn_entity. Omit and the NPC behaves as a villager.

description.description: NPCs: what this character LOOKS LIKE, in Spanish, one line ('herrero fornido con mandil de cuero quemado'). It is the prompt that paints their AI skin, so describe appearance — build, clothes, tools, hair — not biography. Without it the skin is painted from their proper name, which describes nobody. Always write one for a named NPC.

style_ref.description: NPCs only, optional: id of the character reference from world.style_refs.characters that best matches this NPC's look (guides the AI skin). Missing/unknown id falls back to a role-derived default.
